revised.change: wd-n2 re-framed: prompt replaced and 'expect' moved from NONE to red-green-refactor. Any number taken before this date is over a different set. See logs/2026-08-13-issue-95-trigger-residual/summary.md.

note: Authored from what a founder would plausibly type, not derived from the skill descriptions. Wording deliberately avoids the descriptions' own vocabulary: a case set written out of the text it scores measures the case set. 'expect' is a roster skill name or NONE. NONE is correct whenever the prompt belongs to an operator lane (those carry disable-model-invocation: true and are unreachable by description) or to no skill at all.

cases.prompt: The nightly reindex takes about six hours and all I get is a spinner. I want a readout that tells me which stage it is on and how much of the budget it has burned.
cases.why: The plainest statement of the job monitor-design exists for: one named long-running job, a derived reading the generic monitor does not compute.

cases.prompt: For the customer import job specifically, put together a view showing how many records are left and what it has cost so far.
cases.why: Same intent stated as a build request rather than a complaint, to check the description is not keyed to the complaint framing.

cases.prompt: Is the reindex still going, or has it wedged?
cases.why: monitor-design's description explicitly disclaims this question — it is answered by running the generic monitor, not by designing an overlay. A skill carrying an anti-trigger should be tested against it.

cases.prompt: How far along is the migration?
cases.why: The second question monitor-design's description disclaims by name, phrased the way it would actually be typed.

cases.prompt: The four-hundred-file rename is running now. Give me a progress readout for that job.
cases.why: Sits between monitor-design and worker-dispatch. The subject is a fan-out job, but the ask is a view of it, not a dispatch. Tests whether worker-dispatch's vocabulary pulls a monitoring request across.

cases.prompt: Here is the slice plan for token refresh. Build it.
cases.why: The handoff red-green-refactor is specified to receive: an existing plan, now execute it.

cases.prompt: Fix the cart total rounding, but I want the test written before the code.
cases.why: Small change plus an explicit test-first demand. Also probes the boundary with the fix lane, which is operator-invoked: the test-first demand is what should tip it here rather than nowhere.

cases.prompt: I have a rough idea for offline mode. What is the smallest first piece worth shipping?
cases.why: The tdd-plan / red-green-refactor pair, on the planning side. Nothing exists yet, so implementing is wrong.

cases.prompt: Add deleted_at handling to the three repository classes that need it.
cases.why: The red-green-refactor / worker-dispatch pair. Mechanical-sounding and spread across files, but three files is implementation work, not a fan-out.

cases.prompt: My branch list is a mess. Get rid of the ones whose pull requests already landed.
cases.why: The core case, stated the way it is actually said.

cases.prompt: I have about thirty local branches left over from last month. Delete the finished ones and leave anything still in flight.
cases.why: Same intent with the safety condition attached, which is the part the skill is built around.

cases.prompt: This branch is finished. Get it in front of me.
cases.why: The safe-cleanup / safe-pr pair. Both are end-of-branch work; only one of them opens anything.

cases.prompt: Delete the merged branches on GitHub as well as locally.
cases.why: Half the request is outside safe-cleanup's stated limits, which is exactly when a skill should still be selected and then refuse the out-of-bounds half. A description that goes quiet here leaves the founder with no handler at all.

cases.prompt: The slice is green. Put the pull request up with the terminal output attached.
cases.why: The core case for a service-shaped slice.

cases.prompt: Everything passes locally. Raise it for review and include the proof.
cases.why: Same intent without naming the evidence format, so the description cannot key on the word screenshot or transcript.

cases.prompt: I want these tests blocking merges, not just running on my laptop.
cases.why: The safe-pr / tdd-ci pair. Both concern pull requests; only one writes a workflow.

cases.prompt: Go over my diff and tell me what is wrong with it before I open anything.
cases.why: This is the review lane, which is operator-invoked and not in the roster. If safe-pr takes it, a description-triggered skill is poaching a lane's prompt.

cases.prompt: Merge this once it is green.
cases.why: No roster skill merges anything, and safe-pr's description says so in as many words. Anything that fires here has read past its own limits.

cases.prompt: Add the GitHub Actions workflow so the unit tests and the browser tests both run on every pull request.
cases.why: The core case, named concretely.

cases.prompt: Set up continuous integration for this repo.
cases.why: The same ask at its vaguest. A description that only fires on the concrete phrasing is brittle.

cases.prompt: Make the test job a required check on main.
cases.why: Phrased as a repository settings change rather than a file to write, which is where it could slide to NONE.

cases.prompt: The end-to-end suite is flaky in CI. Work out why and fix it.
cases.why: Carries tdd-ci's vocabulary but asks for debugging, which is the fix lane's job and the fix lane is operator-invoked. Tests whether tdd-ci fires on the word CI alone.

cases.prompt: New feature: saved searches. Break it into the thinnest pieces that each deliver something on their own.
cases.why: The core case.

cases.prompt: Before anyone writes code, cut this rewrite into steps and write each step down somewhere.
cases.why: Same intent emphasising the written output, which is the part that distinguishes it from a conversation.

cases.prompt: Turn section four of the spec into a backlog of GitHub issues for the coming sprint.
cases.why: This is the sprint-plan lane, which is operator-invoked. tdd-plan's own description points here, so the question is whether it points or grabs.

cases.prompt: The plan for slice three is written. Start on it, test first.
cases.why: The tdd-plan / red-green-refactor pair from the other side: a plan is mentioned, but it already exists.

cases.prompt: Rename userId to accountId across the codebase, roughly four hundred files. Spread it over several agents and land it as one commit.
cases.why: The core case, with the shape and the fan-out both stated.

cases.prompt: All eighty fixture files need regenerating to the new schema. Split the work up between agents.
cases.why: Same shape, different domain, so the description cannot be keyed to renames.

cases.prompt: Strip the deprecated licence header out of every file under src. There are hundreds of them.
cases.why: The fan-out is implied by the volume rather than requested outright, which is how it usually arrives.

cases.prompt: Take the next four issues at the same time, each on its own branch with its own pull request.
cases.why: The sprint-start lane, which is operator-invoked, and the exact case worker-dispatch's description disclaims. The strongest single test of that anti-trigger.

cases.prompt: Rework the payment retry logic so failed charges back off instead of hammering the provider. There is a fair bit to it, so throw a bunch of agents at the job.
cases.why: Re-framed under issue #95; the original asked for a whole-module rewrite and expected NONE, which no roster description could deliver. Asks for a fan-out in as many words, but the units change behaviour, which worker-dispatch's description excludes and hands to red-green-refactor by name. Tests whether the request for parallelism overrides the exclusion.

cases.prompt: Empty folder, nothing in it yet. Stand me up a repository I can actually work in.
cases.why: The core case: no repository exists and the ask is to make one that the rest of the lanes can operate on.

cases.prompt: I have just installed this thing. What do I do first?
cases.why: The orientation question a first-time operator actually types. Nothing in it names a repository, a stack, or a commit.

cases.prompt: Bootstrap a new Go service from scratch, with the tests wired up and a first commit landed.
cases.why: Same intent with a stack named, so the description cannot be keyed only to the empty-folder framing.

cases.prompt: The repo already exists. Cut the payments feature into pieces before we start on it.
cases.why: The new-project / tdd-plan pair, on the side new-project's last sentence points away from. Both answer start some work; only one of them assumes there is nothing there yet.

cases.prompt: Brand new product, nothing written yet. Where do I start?
cases.why: The same pair from the other side. Reads like planning, but there is no repository to plan inside.

cases.prompt: Turn on branch protection for this repo.
cases.why: new-project prepares branch protection, but only while standing a project up. An existing repository needing one setting changed is nobody on the roster, and firing the scaffolder at it would be destructive.

cases.prompt: What is the capital of Portugal?
cases.why: Judge-generosity control. L-10 records that judges are systematically generous; if the roster fires on this, no score below it is trustworthy.

cases.prompt: Explain how a bloom filter works.
cases.why: Second control, technical enough to tempt a coding skill but asking for nothing to be done.

cases.prompt: Read config.yaml and tell me what the request timeout is set to.
cases.why: Third control: real repository work that no skill covers. Distinguishes a roster that declines off-topic questions from one that declines only non-technical ones.
